name: Overhead / Smash
summary: The overhead is how you finish a ball that has been lobbed or popped up above your head. The shot itself is not hard — the footwork under it is. Most missed overheads are missed because the player never got behind the ball.
whenToUse: A dink has popped up high enough that you can take it above your head.
You have been lobbed and can get behind the ball rather than reaching back for it.
The opponents are both at the kitchen line, so a ball at their feet ends the rally.
You are inside the transition zone or closer — from the baseline the angle is not there.
howTo: Turn sideways immediately and move with side-steps, not by backpedalling.
Get behind the ball so it drops in front of your hitting shoulder, not on top of your head.
Point at the ball with your free hand to keep the tracking honest.
Reach up and contact it high with a snap from the shoulder and wrist.
Hit down at a gap or at their feet, not at maximum pace.
Recover forward to the kitchen line — a defended overhead comes back short.
commonMistakes: Backpedalling with your feet square, which is both slow and how people land on their backs.
Letting the ball get behind your head, so the smash goes into the net or straight up.
Swinging as hard as possible at a ball that only needed to be placed.
Smashing from the baseline, where every angle is covered and the ball comes back.
Watching it and standing still instead of moving in behind it.

drills.name: Side-step and smash
drills.description: Your partner lobs deliberately from the kitchen. You turn sideways and side-step back under it — no backpedalling allowed. If your feet ever square up, that repetition does not count.

drills.name: Place it, do not crush it
drills.description: Same lob feed, but score only smashes that land inside their kitchen. Anything hit hard and deep scores nothing, however satisfying it was.
